purpose: Machine-readable theorem/claim registry. One record per theorem, lemma, counterexample, structural result, certificate, or unresolved claim. Use dependencies/implies edges as a theorem dependency graph; use proof_location to open the detailed mathematical statement in KNOWN_RESULTS.md or OPEN_PROBLEMS.md.

status_definitions.bridge: Direct synthesis or translation of established results into ScoreQuant notation/problem.
status_definitions.project_proved: Derived in the project and currently treated as proved internally; not yet publication-audited.
status_definitions.counterexample: An explicit example falsifies the stated/generalized claim.
status_definitions.search_gap: Targeted literature search found no direct precedent; not a novelty claim.
status_definitions.measured: Supported by empirical/regression evidence only (see NUMERICAL_EVIDENCE.md); not a proof.

publication_status_definitions.published: Result is attributed to external published literature.
publication_status_definitions.internal: Internal project result; requires external proof/prior-art audit.

literature_search_status_definitions.not_searched: No targeted prior-art search has been run for this claim.
literature_search_status_definitions.search_gap: Targeted prior-art search found no direct precedent; recorded in LITERATURE.md; not a novelty claim.
literature_search_status_definitions.prior_art_found: Direct or near-direct precedent located; see the literature entry cited by the claim.

claims.title: Quantized Fisher-information identity
claims.statement: For Z=q(S), the categorical score is E[S|Z] and I_q=Var(E[S|Z])=Σ_b W_b μ_b μ_b^T=Σ_b m_b m_b^T/W_b.
assumptions: quantizer fixed with respect to theta when differentiating

claims.title: Exact Fisher-information loss decomposition
claims.statement: I_full-I_q=E[Cov(S|Z)] is positive semidefinite; hard quantization cannot increase Fisher information.

claims.title: Local Fisher-losslessness iff the score is bin-measurable
claims.statement: I_q=I_full iff S=h(Z) almost surely, equivalently Cov(S|Z)=0 almost surely.

claims.title: Rank ceiling for K hard categories
claims.statement: rank(I_q)<=min(d,K-1); positive-definite full-D information requires K>=d+1.

claims.title: Refinement monotonicity
claims.statement: If partition P' refines P then I_P' >= I_P in Loewner order.

claims.title: D-optimal partition invariance under invertible reparameterization
claims.statement: Under an invertible local parameter transformation, I_q transforms by congruence and logdet changes only by a quantizer-independent constant.

claims.title: Normalized retained-information spectrum
claims.statement: R=I_full^{-1/2} I_q I_full^{-1/2} satisfies 0<=R<=I, so every retention eigenvalue lies in [0,1].

claims.title: Normalized trace equals Fisher-whitened k-means
claims.statement: d-tr(I_full^{-1}I_q)=E||z-E[z|Z]||^2 for z=I_full^{-1/2}s; maximizing retained normalized trace is weighted k-means.

proof_location.section: T1. Fisher-whitened normalized trace equals weighted k-means

claims.warning: This control case is known in substance and is not a novelty claim.

claims.title: Infinitesimal cell-transfer identity
claims.statement: Moving infinitesimal mass from cell a to b gives dI=[(s-μ_a)(s-μ_a)^T-(s-μ_b)(s-μ_b)^T]dε; for differentiable F the directional derivative is the difference of the corresponding G=∇F(I) quadratic forms.

claims.title: Concavity/supergradient finite-move screening
claims.statement: For concave F and any supergradient G, exact finite relocation satisfies ΔF <= tr(GΔI)=α u_a^T G u_a-β u_b^T G u_b. Non-positive weighted tangent gain safely rejects the move.
claims.role: criterion-generic safe pruning and sufficient stability certificate

claims.title: Weighted tangent stability implies exchange stability
claims.statement: If every admissible move has weighted tangent gain <=0 for a valid criterion supergradient, no exact one-point move can improve the objective.

claims.title: Refinement upper bounds for Loewner-monotone criteria
claims.statement: Any Loewner-monotone criterion can use information from a refinement as an upper bound on any coarser completion.

claims.title: Population stationary D geometry
claims.statement: A regular atomless stationary D quantizer assigns almost every score to a nearest centroid in the common metric I_q^{-1}; pairwise boundaries are affine hyperplanes.
assumptions: no relevant boundary mass for pointwise statement

claims.title: Exact weighted rank-two relocation
claims.statement: For a weighted point moved from non-singleton a to b, ΔI=αu_a u_a^T-βu_b u_b^T with α=wW_a/(W_a-w), β=wW_b/(W_b+w).

claims.title: Exact finite D log-determinant gain
claims.statement: With H=I^{-1}, q_aa=u_a^T H u_a, q_bb=u_b^T H u_b, q_ab=u_a^T H u_b, the determinant ratio is (1+αq_aa)(1-βq_bb)+αβq_ab^2.
assumptions: current and candidate information positive definite

claims.title: D leverage inequality
claims.statement: For every centroid μ_c, μ_c^T I^{-1}μ_c<=1/W_c, and for δ=μ_a-μ_b, δ^T I^{-1}δ<=1/W_a+1/W_b.
claims.role: key inequality in finite D geometry

claims.title: Finite D exchange stability implies strict self-consistent Voronoi
claims.statement: For distinct positive-weight score atoms obtained by merging duplicate rows, positive-definite retained information, exactly K nonempty cells, no move constraints beyond preserving nonempty cells, and zero-tolerance exact stability, every tied-or-worse nearest-centroid comparison from a non-singleton source has strictly positive exact D gain. Stability forces distinct centroids; singleton rows are then strictly nearest to their own centroids. Hence one-point exchange stability implies strict self-consistent D-Voronoi geometry.
assumptions: coincident score rows merged, or labels constant on every duplicate class
no relocation constraints beyond preserving nonempty cells

claims.title: Split duplicate atoms defeat strict D-Voronoi closure
claims.statement: If coincident positive-weight score atoms may occupy different singleton cells, a positive-definite labeling can be vacuously one-point exchange stable while strict nearest-centroid assignment and deterministic score-only label reproduction fail.

proof_location.section: CE-D-UNMERGED-DUPLICATES-001 — split duplicate atoms block strict D-Voronoi closure

claims.role: boundary condition for the finite D theorem and compiler

claims.title: Quantitative D gain lower bound for a Voronoi violation
claims.statement: For the theorem-triggering violation, ΔF_D >= log(1+αβ q_delta^2/4)>0 for distinct centroids.

proof_location.section: D5. Exchange stability implies strict D-Voronoi geometry

claims.title: Exact finite inductive closure / compiler
claims.statement: Every exact zero-tolerance one-point-exchange-stable positive-definite finite D solution on merged distinct positive-weight score atoms compiles to q_hat(s)=argmin_b (s-μ_b)^T I_hat^{-1}(s-μ_b), reproducing all merged-atom training labels strictly; original duplicate rows inherit the merged label. Positive solver tolerance gives only a tolerance-stamped boundary-disagreement guarantee.

proof_location.section: D6. Exact finite inductive closure / compiler

claims.role: bridge from finite assignment to deployable classifier

claims.title: Every finite global D optimum is geometrically realizable
claims.statement: Every finite global D optimum is exchange stable and therefore strict self-consistent D-Voronoi; unrestricted finite D optimization and realizable affine/Voronoi labeling optimization have the same optimum value.

proof_location.section: D7. Every finite global D optimum is geometrically realizable

claims.title: Monotone exact D one-point exchange
claims.statement: Accepting only exact positive D gains strictly increases the objective, cannot cycle, and terminates finitely at a one-point exchange-stable state.

claims.title: Adaptive Mahalanobis Lloyd need not increase D
claims.statement: Batch recomputation of I^{-1}, nearest-centroid reassignment, and centroid update can decrease the true logdet objective.

proof_location.section: D9. Adaptive Mahalanobis Lloyd is not monotone

claims.title: Guarded D-Lloyd proposal is monotone when accepted by exact objective
claims.statement: A batch Lloyd/Voronoi reassignment may be used as a proposal, but monotonicity is restored only by accepting proposals that improve the exact D objective.

proof_location.section: D9. Adaptive Mahalanobis Lloyd is not monotone

claims.title: D-Voronoi fixed point does not imply exchange stability
claims.statement: Self-consistent nearest-centroid assignment under the current D metric is strictly weaker than one-point exact exchange stability.

proof_location.section: D10. Voronoi fixed point does not imply exchange stability

claims.title: Exact finite D optimization is XP for fixed (d,K)
claims.statement: Because global optima are affine/Voronoi-realizable, arrangement enumeration yields an exact algorithm N^{O(Kd)} for fixed d and K.

proof_location.section: D11. Exact global enumeration for fixed \((d,K)\)

claims.warning: This is XP-style, not an FPT result; hardness and tightness remain open.

claims.title: Singleton-refinement branch-and-bound upper bound for D
claims.statement: For unassigned U, I_completion <= I_partial+Σ_{i∈U} w_i s_i s_i^T, so its logdet is a valid upper bound on every completion.

claims.title: Safe D tangent screening
claims.statement: For G=I^{-1}, a non-positive weighted tangent gain guarantees non-positive exact D gain.

claims.title: Classical Ds optimal-design theory
claims.statement: Classical optimal-design theory supplies Ds/subset criteria, Schur-complement formulations, sensitivity/equivalence theorems, and nuisance-parameter tools.
claims.warning: The design feasible set differs from hard score-space partitioning.

claims.title: Ds objective is the logdet of efficient/profiled Schur information
claims.statement: For POI ψ and nuisance λ, S_ψ(I)=I_ψψ-I_ψλ I_λλ^{-1} I_λψ and F_s=logdet S_ψ(I)=logdet I-logdet I_λλ when the relevant blocks are nonsingular.

claims.title: Ds first-order gradient is an efficient semimetric
claims.statement: For regular nonsingular blocks, G_s=I^{-1}-E_λ I_λλ^{-1} E_λ^T is positive semidefinite of rank d_ψ and induces the population first-order efficient-score semimetric.

claims.title: Exact finite Ds one-point objective oracle
claims.statement: The full information has the universal rank-two update and exact profiled gain is Δlogdet I-Δlogdet I_λλ, giving an exact low-rank finite move oracle when blocks stay nonsingular.

proof_location.section: DS3. Exact finite one-point objective oracle

claims.title: Monotone exact Ds exchange terminates finitely
claims.statement: Accepting only exact positive Ds gains on a finite labeling set yields strict ascent and finite termination at a one-point exchange-stable state.

proof_location.section: DS3. Exact finite one-point objective oracle

claims.title: Safe Ds tangent screening
claims.statement: A non-positive weighted tangent gain under the valid Ds gradient/supergradient safely rejects an exact finite move.

claims.title: D-style finite exchange-to-geometry theorem fails for Ds
claims.statement: Positive first-order efficient-semimetric margin need not imply positive exact finite Ds gain; exchange stability does not force exact finite efficient-Voronoi assignment.

proof_location.section: DS4. D-style finite geometry theorem fails

claims.title: A finite global Ds optimum can be non-geometric
claims.statement: An exact centered equal-weight N=8,d=2,d_ψ=1,K=3 exhaustive example has a unique global Ds optimum that violates its own efficient-semimetric nearest-cell rule.

proof_location.section: DS5. A global finite \(D_s\) optimum can be non-geometric

claims.title: Approximate finite Ds efficient-Voronoi necessity bound
claims.statement: At a one-point exchange-stable Ds state, relative first-order violation is bounded by w_i(1/W_a+1/W_b); for equal weights and balanced cells this is O(K/N).

claims.title: Full-data efficient-score domination
claims.statement: For full-data efficient score S_hat=S_ψ-B* S_λ, every quantizer satisfies Schur_ψ(I_q) <= Var(E[S_hat|q(S)]) in Loewner order.
assumptions: full-data nuisance block regular enough to define B*

claims.title: D-optimal efficient-score quantization upper-bounds global Ds
claims.statement: Taking determinants/suprema in efficient-score domination yields a lower-dimensional D-optimal quantization problem whose optimum is an upper bound on the globally optimal in-bin Ds value.

claims.title: Scalar efficient-score upper problem is exactly solvable by dynamic programming
claims.statement: For d_ψ=1, deterministic D-optimal quantization of a scalar efficient score has ordered interval cells, and the finite-sample optimum can be solved exactly by dynamic programming.

proof_location.section: DS8. Scalar efficient-score upper problem is exactly solvable by DP

claims.role: cheap global upper certificate and initializer

claims.title: Full in-bin Ds profiling is singular when K<=d
claims.statement: Because rank(I_q)<=K-1, ordinary full-block in-bin Ds profiling is not identifiable when K<=d.

claims.title: Projected efficient-score problem only requires K>=d_ψ+1
claims.statement: When nuisance information is supplied externally via full-data efficient-score projection, the lower-dimensional projected D problem structurally requires only K>=d_ψ+1.
claims.warning: This is a different statistical formulation from full in-bin nuisance profiling.

claims.title: E-optimality supergradient structure
claims.statement: For F_E(I)=lambda_min(I), a simple minimum eigenvalue has gradient vv^T; with multiplicity r the superdifferential is {VHV^T:H>=0,tr H=1}.

claims.title: Repeated minimum eigenvalues make one-transfer first-order E geometry non-identifying
claims.statement: For a one-transfer rank-two direction and minimum eigenspace dimension r>=2, the directional derivative is <=0; one-point first-order stability can become automatic at the degeneracy.

claims.title: Finite global E optimum can violate its own rank-one nearest-cell rule
claims.statement: An exhaustive finite example with a simple minimum eigenvalue has a global E optimum whose vv^T nearest-cell rule disagrees with a training label.

claims.title: Soft assignments are an actual randomized quantizer
claims.statement: For probabilities r_ib, W_b=Σ_i w_i r_ib and m_b=Σ_i w_i r_ib s_i give I_soft=Σ_b m_bm_b^T/W_b, the Fisher information of the corresponding randomized categorical observation when the randomization rule is theta-independent.

claims.title: Exact soft-assignment gradient
claims.statement: For differentiable F with G=∇F(I_soft), ∂F/∂r_ib=w_i(2 s_i^T G μ_b-μ_b^T G μ_b), equivalent up to a bin-independent term to negative squared G-distance.

claims.title: Hard finite geometric objective is piecewise constant in boundary parameters

claims.title: Fixed-temperature soft optimization has standard nonconvex stationary guarantees
claims.statement: A positive-temperature softmax affine-max family is smooth on the regular region; line-search gradient/quasi-Newton methods can be monotone in the soft objective and converge only to standard stationary notions.

claims.title: Atomless purification preserves (W_b,m_b)
claims.statement: For an atomless score law and finite labels, Dvoretzky-Wald-Wolfowitz purification can preserve all cell probabilities and first score moments of a randomized quantizer.

claims.title: Randomized and deterministic population optima coincide for moment-based criteria under atomlessness
claims.statement: Because the objectives depend only on (W_b,m_b), atomless purification implies randomized and deterministic quantizers have the same attainable population objective values.

claims.title: Restricted affine-max empirical consistency
claims.statement: For a compact finite-capacity affine-max class with uniform cell-mass and conditioning margins and appropriate score integrability, cell moments converge uniformly; objective values converge uniformly; approximate empirical maximizers are value-consistent, and isolated population optima give decision/parameter consistency up to labels.
assumptions: required information eigenvalues bounded away from zero
bounded scores or suitable uniform integrability
claims.warning: The unrestricted/global consistency problem remains open.

claims.title: Local score can be obtained from a local density ratio

claims.title: Linear-mixture component ratios suffice for score construction

read_order: README.md defines the single canonical read order; follow it rather than any local copy.
rules: Locate the target claim by id or by criterion/status/level index.
Follow dependencies recursively before attempting a proof.
Open proof_location for the full mathematical statement and assumptions.
Treat project_proved as an internal dependency, not a published fact.
Treat counterexample nodes as hard blockers to stronger generalized claims.
Patch this registry after every theorem investigation.
